overview: This file concerns Nichols Engineering & Research Corporation’s effort to obtain technical and operating data about flash roasters it had designed in 1940 for a Japanese sulfuric-acid installation associated with Mitsui and Toyo Koatsu Kogyo K.K. The State Department identified the probable plant as the 50,000-metric-ton-capacity facility at Sunagawa, Hokkaido, but explained that it had only begun limited operation in 1946, that the use of Nichols’s designs could not be confirmed, and that Occupation engineering personnel could not yet undertake the requested study. Fragmentary internal notes discuss the possible installation of three roasters, doubts about whether flash-roaster equipment was actually used, and possible ways to refer the inquiry to officials in Japan. A final 1948 transfer sheet records the refiling of a Nanjing telegram under a Japan-related decimal-file number, although the telegram itself is absent.

subfiles.title: Nichols Engineering request for data on Japanese flash roasters
subfiles.from: R. W. Rowen, Nichols Engineering & Research Corporation
subfiles.to: Far East Division, U.S. Department of State
subfiles.about: Nichols requests extensive technical information about flash roasters and associated sulfuric-acid equipment believed to have been installed for Toyo Koatsu Kogyo in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Nichols asks State for operating data on flash-roaster furnaces it designed for Mitsui's Japanese plant in 1940.

subfiles.title: State Department reply on the Sunagawa sulfuric-acid plant
subfiles.from: Roswell H. Whitman, Division of Japanese and Korean Economic Affairs
subfiles.to: R. W. Rowen, Nichols Engineering & Research Corporation
subfiles.about: Whitman identifies Sunagawa as the probable site but declines to commission the requested engineering investigation while the plant remains in limited initial operation.
subfiles.summary: State reports the probable Sunagawa plant began operating only in 1946, well below capacity, and can't confirm the flash-roaster design was installed.

subfiles.title: Internal memorandum and handwritten notes on handling the Nichols inquiry
subfiles.about: Fragmentary internal notes assess available plant information and propose alternatives for referring or answering Nichols’s inquiry.
subfiles.summary: Notes debate who should handle Nichols's inquiry on the Japanese plant, suggesting it be referred through Atcheson.

subfiles.title: Transfer sheet for Nanjing telegram no. 1383
subfiles.about: The sheet records the transfer of a July 29, 1948 telegram from Nanjing to another State Department decimal-file classification.
subfiles.summary: Transfer sheet records a 1948 Nanjing telegram's filing, with its content not preserved.

interest: Shows a US firm's 1946 bid to recover Japanese data on sulfuric-acid plants built from prewar American designs.
